answer: A harbor can limit how many ships dock at once, and an agent economy can do the same with payout lanes. Each new identity starts in a narrow lane with a tiny earnings cap, and the cap widens only as its grades match jury verdicts over many epochs. A sybil farmer must run every fake account through that slow climb, so a thousand identities earn roughly what one does, and reaching the zenith lane costs weeks of honest judging per account, which wipes out the profit. A violet flag on mismatched graders freezes their lane.
